note: CHANGES NUMBERS on fast designs with AIRFOIL fins. On the default model (Rogers Kbf) a sharp airfoil fin is no longer charged the blunt leading-edge pressure drag classic Barrowman applies to every non-square cross-section — a swept-cylinder plateau of ~1.2 on the leading-edge frontal area that neither decays with Mach nor belongs on a sharp section. Total drag falls under 1% below Mach 0.5, ~4-12% at Mach 0.9 and 9-16% at Mach 2 on the reference designs, and apogee moves further: a Mach 1.9 test design went 2,227 m to 2,702 m, up 21%. Checked artifact-against-artifact across Mach 0.1-3.0: the Classic Extended Barrowman model (desktop parity) and the Supersonic model are both bit-for-bit unchanged, as are SQUARE (the default) and ROUNDED fins in every model, and any fin naming a specific supersonic airfoil section. Set a design's fins to ROUNDED to keep the old numbers — that is what the classic term actually models. Stated plainly: this moves away from Buckeye's measured apogee (already over-predicted ~12%) and toward the same flight's GPS-derived drag trace (which says the model reads drag 22-42% high supersonic); those two anchors have disagreed since the model was built. The validation harness cannot arbitrate it — every finned fixture names an airfoil section and takes the other path — so all three model scores are unchanged at 10, 17 and 71 of 175.
